title: A buyer's payment exists only in a notification
mechanism_summary: A supposed buyer sends a seller a fake payment notification. The seller may release the item despite receiving no real payment.
suggested_beats: A buyer claims payment is complete.
Only a notification supports the claim.
Check the actual account before releasing goods.
why_it_works: An official-looking notification can substitute for checking the balance.

title: An accidental overpayment requires a real refund
mechanism_summary: A buyer sends an oversized counterfeit check and requests a refund. The seller loses the returned money when the check fails.
suggested_beats: A buyer appears to overpay.
The seller is asked to refund the excess.
Do not refund an unverified check overpayment.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone accepting a check for an online sale
why_it_works: A visible deposit can be mistaken for a final payment.

title: A retail barcode pays a fake utility bill
mechanism_summary: An unexpected caller threatens utility shutoff and sends a barcode for payment at a shop. The barcode instruction is part of an impersonation scam.
suggested_beats: A caller threatens disconnection.
Payment must use a supplied barcode.
Call the utility through details on a genuine bill.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone worried about losing essential service
why_it_works: An urgent service threat makes an unusual payment method seem necessary.

title: A caller supplies the destination at a crypto ATM
mechanism_summary: An impersonator directs someone to a cryptocurrency ATM and supplies a QR code. The code routes the transfer to the scammer's wallet.
suggested_beats: A caller creates an urgent money problem.
The ATM transfer uses the caller's code.
Do not follow unsolicited crypto-payment instructions.
why_it_works: Step-by-step coaching leaves little room to reconsider the destination.

title: A familiar supplier suddenly changes payment details
mechanism_summary: Attackers compromise or imitate business correspondence to redirect a legitimate payment. The payer sends funds to an account supplied by the impostor.
suggested_beats: A familiar business payment is due.
Email changes where the money should go.
Confirm changed payment instructions through a known contact.
why_it_works: An existing business relationship makes substituted instructions look routine.

title: An invoice bills for unordered supplies
mechanism_summary: A business receives a fake invoice for routine supplies. Scammers hope staff pay it without confirming that anything was ordered.
suggested_beats: An ordinary-looking invoice arrives.
No matching purchase can be found.
Match invoices to verified orders.
why_it_works: Familiar paperwork exploits habitual payment processing.

title: A payment-app message impersonates a friend
mechanism_summary: A scammer poses as someone the recipient knows and requests money through a payment app. The transfer goes to the impostor.
suggested_beats: A familiar-looking contact asks for help.
The request moves straight to payment.
Confirm the request through a separate trusted channel.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone using payment apps with friends
why_it_works: Social trust can shorten the pause before an irreversible transfer.

title: An assistant job sends a counterfeit check
mechanism_summary: A supposed employer sends a counterfeit check for gift cards. The scammer spends the codes before the check fails.
suggested_beats: A new employer sends advance funds.
The assignment requires sharing gift-card codes.
Do not spend an unknown employer's check on gift cards.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone starting an online assistant job
why_it_works: A job assignment makes sending value to a stranger feel like work.
